title: The Preservation of the Righteous and the Nature of Divine Justice
english: He is not an angel sent to rescue from evils, but the indicated Savior (Ps 33:9a). Regarding God, the good means the same as the good. Since he is also the bread of life, the Spirit commands those who do not have desire for it not to be overwhelmed by it, but only to taste it. For the tasting is sufficient to make them desirous and to make them desire to experience it. And to taste signifies, as if by a little, to know and to examine concerning God. For he says that a pure tasting imparts to the souls an incomparable enjoyment of those things which are above human and wonderful (Ps 33:9b).

Blessed is the man who hopes in him (Ps 33:9b). The man who exists by hoping in God completely and without fail is blessed (Ps 33:10). We say that fear is twofold. For immediately, someone coming to God, having taken up fear toward him, makes straight all his commandments. For it is said: Fear God and keep his commandments (Ps 33:10). But in the present verse, concerning a fear that has ascended above, he speaks of that on which he calls the saints to have become; for having taken on the introductory fear, they hurried toward holiness. But now, he commands those saints not to fear God, but to have the fear that fulfills all good, so that the one having it may be unceasing (Ps 33:12b).

It is to be noted that, just as other good things are taught, so also the divine fear is taught, from which we learn not to signify a passion-driven fear; for an undidactic fear exists by nature not only in humans but also in irrational animals (Ps 33:12b). Since those looking upon the whole of God—powers called eyes in a figurative sense—look upon the righteous, but also his ears are ready to receive their petition, for this reason he says: if you wish to enjoy these, turning away from evil, do the good (Ps 33:15-16).

Those placing all this thoughtlessly and doing evils as if God were not watching, will encounter punishment, receiving a reminder that God is present to exact judgment upon them (Ps 33:17). And according to this, it is said that the face of God shines upon them, or that how their remembrance shall be destroyed not ever, but from the earth. But blessed is the one whose remembrance is destroyed from the earth; for thus the law shall be written.

His [protection] in the heavens. But the workers of iniquity do evil. The Lord will preserve the bones of the righteous (Ps 33:21), not allowing even by chance for them to be broken, nor for the doctrines of the righteous nor for his own powers to be overturned.

He who sins is deprived of life (Ps 33:22a) as he approaches the keeping of the commandments, falling into evil death. And evil death is that which is contrary to the good life, which inflicts pain upon the subject; for Job was also struck with evil, as it is evident that it was inflicting pain. Those who hate what is loved harm not others but themselves (Ps 33:22b). And indeed, the one who hates the diligent righteous man errs and falls into punishment.

It is to be noted what the redemption truly is: it frees souls from captivity; for if bodies are ever redeemed, it is not beforehand but this happens by consequence (Ps 33:23a); and souls are saved, not of others, but of his slaves. Those who hope in the Lord will not be disappointed of the things hoped for and expected (Ps 33:23b).

He also teaches in other places those who fight against him, saying, 'Many are those fighting against me from below' (Ps 34:1bc). Those who were not fighting against him were acting unjustly toward him who had done no injustice; but he does not wish for the enemies to be unpunished, but rather that they be judged by the injustice of the enemies, opposing the justice of God, being destructive against the injustice, just as the light is destructive to the darkness. For injustice, being contrary to and set against the justice of God, will be fought against from it. Therefore also the unrighteous man would be called an enemy to the righteous. But justice makes the righteous a friend to God, just as the just are friends to the just. Therefore it has been said, 'The Lord is righteous and loves righteousness' (Ps 34:1c). The righteous, trusting in his own righteousness, says, 'Judge me, Lord, and judge my case' (Ps 34:1d). The Lord is therefore judging those who do injustice, destroying the injustice within them. And he also fights against those who fight against the righteous, doing this for the good of those being fought against, as if they might at some time cease by practicing righteousness (Ps 34:1b).
The act of doing injustice signifies harm in the [words]: 'Behold, I have given you to tread upon serpents and scorpions and upon...' (Ps 91:13).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Integrity of the Soul and the Power of Prayer
english: [He will protect you from] all the power of the enemy, and he will not wrong you in any way. Since many have set out to fight me through false doctrine and other evils, fight them instead on my behalf; for they shall be irrefutably destroyed, since you are the Lord who crushes wars (Ps 34:2).

Taking hold of your companion's shield and the wealth of truth, 'Arise to my help' (Ps 34:3), that is, become my champion. In the same way, you will think of the sword. It is noteworthy that in the upcoming verses he used imperative words instead of optative ones; for 'Let their way be made' (Gen 7:21) instead of 'May their way be made,' and 'Let him come' instead of 'May he come,' and the rest similarly. And 'he shall fall in the snare' (Ps 34:8); for according to their actions, each one is punished.

When these things happen to them, my soul shall rejoice (Ps 34:9), seeing by providence the wicked being punished and the diligent being benefited; but it will also experience delights, having gained experience of his salvation, of God. Let those who desire to take everything from the bare word and nothing allegorically be rebuked, even from the context of the verse. For it is not foolish to think that the bones possess the thought of God, so as to praise him and know that no one is like him. For concerning the bones of man (and his powers and true doctrines are these), it is said, 'All my bones' (Ps 34:10); for through every thought and true doctrine, I was established that nothing of the created is like the Lord; for he himself is the image of the invisible God and the exact imprint of the divine hypostasis.

Furthermore, whether the poor man is more [distinguished] than the laborer, and whether in hypostasis or in conception, the one who is poor and remains poor, and the one who has fallen from wealth, and the laborer who acquires things through toil to live. Those who, rising up and stirring themselves up as witnesses of injustice rather than justice, ask sophistically, 'I do not know.' For the diligent knows nothing of the wicked, that is, he has not been mixed with any of the evil ones; and a testimony: 'He who keeps the commandment shall not know an evil word' (Prov 14:16). And in

For here the 'will not know' stands instead of 'has not trusted' or 'has not been tested' regarding an evil word. For it is a falsehood to think that one who guards the divine commandment does not know an evil word; for having a discernment of evil and good, he has turned away from all other things to keep the commandment. He does not say such a thing: 'They, interrogating me, seeking to distinguish my lack of experience or knowledge or intention regarding evils, questioned me about them, just as the Egyptians did to Joseph, and the elders to Susanna.' (Ps 34:12).

When I, desiring to perform my duties toward all people blamelessly, wishing to live in peace with all men if possible, they instead returned evil to me for these good things, enemies and ill-wishers appearing through all things; and they attempted to annul in themselves the good fruitfulness of my soul. If, indeed, being persuaded by their questions, I had become such as they wished to make me, my soul would have been rendered barren, no longer receiving the divine marriages of the Bridegroom. But if the disciples of the Teacher were to say, 'and thus the soul of the Teacher is not rendered barren, falling into errors through its own stumbling block, annulling those born from it through discipleship,' [this would be an error].

Because luxury, stirring up irrational pleasures, irrationally exalts the soul, while fasting, doing the opposite, cuts down the passions; but also praiseworthy fasting effects a cleansing of sins, truly working blindness and humbling the soul. For him who has prayed well, the prayer returns to him, bringing back the good things for his sake, and having turned back, it is drawn into the bosom of the one who sent it. And 'the bosom' signifies their ruling principle; for their humiliation was into their bosom in the land of Egypt, and all things come into the bosom of the innocent; and in this way all the righteous go into the bosom of Abraham, that is, into the same mind and promise as he. (Ps 34:13).

I did not lie so pleasingly toward those wishing to harm the things previously mentioned, as if one were pleasing to a neighbor and a closer brother; but not so, as they were not pleasing to me as a neighbor and a closer brother. (Ps 34:14). Since I lied as if concerning genuine brothers...

title: The Nature of Sin and Davidic Conduct
english: Seeing them through whom they act as if dying, I humbled myself by mourning them and frowning upon them, seeking to preserve the one able to keep me harmless from them (Ps 34:15ab).

The present [text] is explanatory if it is possible for [God] to repay me evil for good. For while I mourn and frown over them, through which they possess death, they gather together in joy against me, as if they were to take me by the hand; and they have plotted against me, so that they might gather and rejoice (Ps 34:15c).

Because of those who attempted against me, I was logically scourged in my soul; but I remain harmless, neither perceiving nor knowing those approaching them. If ever, when the enemies were dividing, a disturbance in the thoughts occurred toward sin, so that I was to be scourged by sensations from the thoughts, I did not reveal these lashes to those opposing me, lest they, not taking a starting point from the branch of the soul, should rather attack me (Ps 34:15c-16).

Having gathered and rejoiced against me, they were split apart by divine providence; having been dissolved and scattered in such a way, they did not repent, that is, they did not recognize for whom they had advised wickedly, but instead they attempted the same against others. Because of all those who were striving to make an attempt upon me, they were not able to see or take hold of me; therefore, they turned to mocking and sneering at me. Watching like wild beasts, they bared their teeth, that is, their angry and wrathful power, against me; for wanting to devour me, they failed (Ps 34:16-17).

The holy one says: 'Lord, how long will you look?' (Ps 34:17). For when you look, all the aforementioned things will be gathered together with those doing them. And he says 'only begotten' because his soul has it alone; for one must not pay attention to the myth-making regarding metempsychosis. Perhaps the only begotten besides his soul is the essence of the spirit joined to the soul; for it is only begotten in its separation from all those in us according to divinity (Ps 34:18).

A great assembly is gathered from many saints, a heavy people, the steadfast and solid, praying and interceding (Ps 34:22b). Since you are present with me, the enemies are far; do not depart from me, lest they come upon me alone (Ps 34:22b).

Because God's long-suffering is often called his breath (Ps 34:23), the Lord is driven to indignation by the pressing of enemies, saying: 'Arise, Lord, and take up my judgment,' that is, stand up with the power of your strength, so that the things concerning me against my enemies may be examined. For this is for good, since they hate me unjustly and those who hate me without cause shall certainly be condemned (Ps 34:27-28).

And not everyone, the writer, took the psalm toward David and toward Christ, but rather toward Christ; another [took it] indistinctly toward the righteous; and the third toward David alone. Regarding the overcoming of enemies, one says it is spoken prophetically of things that will happen, while the other says it is for the benefit of the enemies, that these things be said so that they might be ashamed, be trapped, and receive sensation of their own sins and retreat from the way they feared. The third says that David lives a legalistic and not an evangelical life; for the law, he says, forbids loving the neighbor and hating the enemy, and speaking badly; for David, living evangelically, says, 'If I repaid evil to those repaying evil to me' (Ps 35:2). Finally, not everyone says these things were spoken prophetically as that he would certainly be.

He who considers himself lawless in himself says nothing other than that he sins. For someone, having first agreed in thought, proceeds to sin in practice. He can also say in himself that he sins, which is 'But if all in your mind...' 'I will ascend into heaven,' and the following. 'If fear is held before the eyes of a man, he abstained from every sin,' but since he does not have it in himself, he says, 'to sin.' A testimony of not sinning for one who has fear is 'That how your fear may come upon you, so that you may not sin' (Ps 35:3).

He who has become lawless, knowing his lawlessness to be hateful; if he were to be observed, he would deceive before Him, so that the shame of the lawlessness might not be found, lest he should hate it. This is what those who reason sophistically do, agreeing with sin as if it were a duty and not something contrary to reason. There is another scripture (Ps 35:4-5).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
